plotting_plan.title: From Item-Level Acquiescence to Model-Level Homogenization
plotting_plan.objective: A four-stage block diagram that visualizes the single-cause causal chain reported in idea.md: (1) Item-level acquiescence (alignment-driven agree-impulse with directional asymmetry IPIP +0.29 vs SD3 -0.33); (2) Reverse-keyed items behave like forward items, deflating Cronbach's alpha (Spearman rho = -1.0 with reverse density); (3) Inflated inter-domain correlations cause EFA to collapse the expected 5-factor Big Five into 3 factors universally; (4) Safety-induced homogenization shrinks inter-model variance to <1%. Arrows connect the stages and a side panel lists the diagnostic battery (4 instruments, 17 domains, 20 LLMs x 17 personas x k=5 = 375,700 API calls). The block diagram should look like a publication-grade conceptual figure.

plotting_plan.title: The Six-Check Psychometric Validation Battery Plus Persona Stress Test
plotting_plan.objective: A schematic flow diagram showing the six validity checks (internal consistency, factor structure, reverse-item consistency, variance decomposition, convergent validity, measurement invariance) applied to the 221-item battery, plus the persona stress test stage (PSD, fidelity, target adherence, plasticity, factorial MBTI main effects). Each check is a box that emits a pass/fail badge — every box for LLMs is red FAIL. Inputs box on the left lists the four instruments and 20 LLMs; outputs box on the right shows the propagated failure cascade.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: An expanding literature administers human personality questionnaires (Big Five, Dark Triad) to large language models and reports the resulting scores as if they reflect genuine traits, with downstream proposals to use LLMs as 'silicon samples' for survey simulation. None of this work establishes the prior measurement question — whether the instruments work at all when applied to LLMs.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: In the human-subjects tradition, an instrument is not trusted until it passes a battery of psychometric checks (internal consistency, factor structure, convergent validity, measurement invariance). On LLMs these checks are almost never run; when run, they fail in a single recognizable pattern that has not been mechanistically explained. Our hypothesis is that the failure cascade traces to one source — alignment-induced acquiescence — and that this directly invalidates downstream uses of LLM personality scores including silicon-sample simulation.
search_directions: Highly cited papers and short reports applying Big Five, Dark Triad, or other personality questionnaires to LLMs and treating the resulting scores as trait measurements (the targets of our critique).
Surveys and review papers on psychometrics, classical test theory, structural equation modeling, factor analysis, and measurement invariance in the human-subjects tradition.
Foundational papers establishing the Big Five (NEO-PI, IPIP-NEO), Dark Triad (SD3), Zuckerman-Kuhlman ZKPQ, and Eysenck EPQR-A inventories that constitute our 4-instrument battery.

Foundational and survey work on response styles, acquiescence bias, and social desirability in survey methodology, as well as the well-established human-subject literature on reverse-keyed items and their use as response-bias detectors.
Influential papers establishing instruction tuning, RLHF/DPO, and constitutional AI as alignment paradigms — the mechanisms we conjecture induce acquiescence on personality questionnaires.
Recent proposals to use LLMs as 'silicon samples' for social-science survey simulation (the downstream application that would inherit any measurement failure).

related_work_strategy.overview: Organize prior work into three methodology clusters that together describe (a) the literature we are critiquing, (b) the human-subject precedent for the validity tests we run, and (c) the technical mechanism we identify as the root cause. For each cluster, find recent SOTA technical work, document the specific limitation it leaves unaddressed, and bridge to how our 6-check + persona-stress evaluation closes that gap.

subsections.bridge_to_our_method: We treat alignment-induced acquiescence and the directional inversion on dark-trait items as the unified mechanism that explains (i) the alpha–reverse-density rank-1 inverse relationship, (ii) the universal 3-factor collapse with Tucker phi = 0.993, (iii) inter-model variance < 1%, (iv) the item-level plasticity dichotomy between visible-behavior items and the alignment safety floor, and (v) persona compliance without measurement validity.

content_bullets: Frame the gap: a fast-growing literature scores LLMs on human personality inventories without first checking that the inventories measure anything on this population.

State the design: 20 LLMs from 8 families, a 221-item battery from 4 validated human inventories (IPIP-NEO-120, SD3, ZKPQ-50-CC, EPQR-A) covering 17 domains and 63 reverse-keyed items, 17 conditions (Default plus 16 MBTI personas), k=5 samples per cell, temperature 0.7, yielding 375,700 raw API calls.

Headline result: every standard validity check fails (alpha tracks reverse-item density at Spearman rho = -1.0; EFA collapses 5 expected Big Five factors into 3 universally with Tucker phi = 0.993; inter-model variance < 1%; mean Default-vs-MBTI item-vector r = 0.461 with 0/320 pairs above r = 0.8).
Mechanism: a single alignment-induced acquiescence with a directional asymmetry (IPIP Delta = +0.29; SD3 Delta = -0.33) drives the whole cascade.

Stress test: persona prompts move profiles by >1 SD (mean PSD = 1.198) with 99.7% nearest-centroid recovery (319/320) but cross-scale coherence is only 0.839 and Fwd/Rev pair coherence 0.696 — role compliance, not measurement validity.

Calibration: LLM observed alphas hug the Random and Pure-Acquiescence synthetic baselines and stay far from the Trait+Acquiescence baseline (alpha > 0.99) — LLMs look like acquiescence with no personality underneath.
Implication: any LLM personality claim must report internal consistency, factor structure, convergent validity, and measurement invariance before interpretation.
Open with the practical stakes: LLM-personality scoring drives behavioral testing, alignment evaluation, and proposals to use LLMs as silicon samples for opinion polling.
Pose the prior measurement question almost never asked: do human instruments measure anything when administered to LLMs?

Introduce the six-check psychometric framework (Cronbach's alpha, factor structure, reverse-item consistency, variance decomposition, convergent validity, measurement invariance) imported from human-subject methodology.

Preview the central empirical finding: every check fails, and every failure traces back to a single alignment-induced acquiescence with a directional asymmetry between normal-personality items (IPIP, Delta = +0.29) and dark-trait items (SD3, Delta = -0.33).

Summarize the cascade: item-level acquiescence inflates inter-domain correlations -> EFA collapses 5 expected factors into 3 universally (Tucker phi = 0.993; replicated under leave-one-model-out, per-family, and per-model) -> inter-model variance falls below 1%, making cross-model personality comparisons statistically meaningless at this resolution.

Preview the persona stress test: MBTI prompts move profiles by >1 SD (mean PSD = 1.198) with 99.7% nearest-centroid recovery, but cross-scale coherence is only 0.839 and Fwd/Rev pair coherence is 0.696, so the 3-factor structure persists inside every persona — role compliance is not the same as trait variance.

Calibration claim: LLM observed alphas sit closest to Random and Pure-Acquiescence simulations and farthest from a Trait+Acquiescence simulation, ruling out 'trait + style noise' as the data-generating process.

List explicit contributions: (i) the first multi-model multi-instrument psychometric VALIDATION study (20 models x 4 instruments x 17 personas x k=5 = 375,700 API calls); (ii) the single-cause causal chain from item to model; (iii) the directional-asymmetry framing that unifies acquiescence and social desirability; (iv) the persona-stress test that documents role compliance without measurement validity; (v) item-level plasticity map of the alignment safety floor; (vi) a methodological prescription for future LLM personality work.
Refer the reader to the teaser causal-chain figure (fig_causal_chain_overview) and the validation-battery schema (fig_validation_battery_schema).

subsections.subsection_title: 3.4 Persona Stress Test and Synthetic Baselines
content_bullets: Persona Separation Degree (PSD): normalized 17-dimensional Euclidean distance from Default in z-score space, divided by sqrt(17).
Nearest-centroid persona classification with leave-one-model-out centroids and metric/scale ablations (z-Euclidean, cosine, Mahalanobis; all/Likert/binary/IPIP-only).
Target adherence: cosine similarity to leave-one-out empirical centroid and to a hand-coded theoretical MBTI target.
Sign-aligned cross-scale coherence on the four overlapping constructs; forward/reverse pair directional coherence.
Item-level plasticity: mean absolute Default-vs-persona shift normalized by scale range.
Factorial main-effects model with two-way interactions across the four MBTI axes (E/I, S/N, T/F, J/P).

subsections.subsection_title: 4.8 Persona Stress Test: Compliance Without Validity
content_bullets: Measurement invariance: mean Pearson r across 320 (model, persona) pairs = 0.461; 0/320 above r = 0.8. Most-invariant ENFJ 0.653, INFJ 0.557, ESFJ 0.528; least-invariant ESTP 0.179, ENTP 0.291, ESFP 0.331. Reference fig_measurement_invariance_histogram.
Persona Separation Degree: mean PSD = 1.198; per-model leaders Gemini-3-Pro 1.384, Gemini-3.1-Pro 1.363, Qwen3-235B 1.344. Reference fig_persona_separation_degree.
Persona fidelity: 99.7% (319/320) nearest-centroid recovery in z-Euclidean; 1.000 in Likert-only; single confusion DeepSeek-V3.2 ESFP -> ENTP. Reference fig_persona_fidelity_confusion_heatmap.
Target adherence: empirical 0.838 [0.791, 0.877]; theoretical 0.557. Strongest ESTP 0.901, weakest INTP 0.699. Reference fig_target_adherence_heatmap.
Cross-scale coherence: overall 0.839; Fwd/Rev pair coherence overall 0.696 (range 0.657 SD3 to 0.737 EPQR-A). Reference fig_cross_scale_coherence_by_construct.
Factorial MBTI main effects: list strongest beta loadings per axis. Reference fig_factorial_mbti_main_effects.
Item-level plasticity: most plastic items 0.5–0.63 (visible-behavior); most locked items 0.000–0.075 (safety/morality). Reference fig_item_plasticity_distribution.
Within-sample stability: vendor SD spans ~10x (Claude-Opus 0.019 to DeepSeek-V4-Pro 0.192); Default is the noisiest persona (0.205). Reference fig_within_sample_consistency_by_model.

Interpretation: persona prompts replace alignment-driven acquiescence with persona-driven compliance — they do not restore measurement validity (3-factor collapse persists inside every persona condition).
Restate the cascade: item-level alignment-driven acquiescence -> alpha collapse along the reverse-density gradient -> universal 3-factor EFA collapse -> sub-1% inter-model variance.
Restate the persona-stress conclusion: 99.7% nearest-centroid recovery vs 0.839 cross-scale coherence and 0.696 Fwd/Rev coherence — role compliance is not measurement validity.

Methodological prescription for future LLM-personality work: always report internal consistency, factor structure, convergent validity, and measurement invariance; establish invariance before cross-condition comparisons; adopt multi-temperature and multi-seed designs to separate stochastic from putative trait variance.
Re-state the directional-asymmetry framing as a unification of sycophancy and safety-driven rejection.
Position the work as a measurement-validity audit that any silicon-sample or LLM-personality study must pass before its scores can be trusted.
Closed-weight API models only — no base / pre-RLHF comparison, so alignment is hypothesized rather than directly isolated.
All instruments and prompts are in English; cross-lingual generalization untested.
Battery is restricted to four self-report inventories; forced-choice, behavioral elicitation, and IRT-fitted alternatives not evaluated.
Temperature is fixed at 0.7 and k = 5; multi-temperature and multi-seed designs are recommended but not run here.
Default 'honest' instruction is one of many no-persona phrasings; alternative no-persona phrasings may shift the implicit role away from ISTJ.
Persona stress test is restricted to the 16 MBTI personas; other persona ontologies untested.
No human subjects; all data are LLM API responses.
Dataset reuse: published, validated human instruments under their original terms.
Public-good motivation: prevent unsupported personality-trait claims about commercial LLMs from propagating into downstream alignment, hiring, or public-opinion applications.
Refusal handling: 61 refusals reported transparently; no attempt to evade safety filters.
Anonymized data and code release deferred to post-acceptance; review version uses anonymous repository placeholders.
